about: Documentation for every mnemonic the assembler's lexer knows, plus the names instructions.json lists. 'format' is a template and 'example' is a line that assembles (branch/jump targets use label_t, la uses a .data label named label_d). Entries with support 'unsupported' do not assemble end to end; 'reason' says why and 'useInstead' names the working spelling, if any. Summaries are RISC-V behaviour checked against this simulator, which is 64-bit only. An entry with a 'caveat' assembles but misbehaves when run; the caveat names the known issue.

lui.summary: Load upper immediate: rd = imm << 12, low 12 bits zero; the result is sign-extended to 64 bits

auipc.summary: Add upper immediate to the PC: rd = pc + (imm << 12), with the shifted immediate sign-extended to 64 bits

jal.summary: Jump and link: rd = address of the next instruction, then jump to label

jalr.summary: Jump and link register: rd = address of the next instruction, then jump to rs1 + imm

beq.summary: Branch to label if rs1 == rs2

bne.summary: Branch to label if rs1 != rs2

blt.summary: Branch to label if rs1 < rs2, signed

bge.summary: Branch to label if rs1 >= rs2, signed

bltu.summary: Branch to label if rs1 < rs2, unsigned

bgeu.summary: Branch to label if rs1 >= rs2, unsigned

lb.summary: Load a byte from rs1 + imm, sign-extended

lh.summary: Load a halfword from rs1 + imm, sign-extended

lw.summary: Load a word from rs1 + imm, sign-extended to the register width

lbu.summary: Load a byte from rs1 + imm, zero-extended

lhu.summary: Load a halfword from rs1 + imm, zero-extended

sb.summary: Store the low byte of rs2 at rs1 + imm

sh.summary: Store the low halfword of rs2 at rs1 + imm

sw.summary: Store the low word of rs2 at rs1 + imm

sltiu.summary: rd = 1 if rs1 < imm (both unsigned; imm is sign-extended first), else 0

slli.summary: Shift rs1 left by a constant, filling with zeros

srli.summary: Shift rs1 right by a constant, filling with zeros

srai.summary: Shift rs1 right by a constant, keeping the sign bit

sll.summary: Shift rs1 left by the low 6 bits of rs2 (this simulator is 64-bit only)

srl.summary: Shift rs1 right by the low 6 bits of rs2, filling with zeros

sra.summary: Shift rs1 right by the low 6 bits of rs2, keeping the sign bit

fence.summary: Order memory accesses before the fence against those after it
fence.reason: Parses, but the code generator has no encoding for it and throws 'Invalid instruction type'.

ecall.summary: Environment call: ask the execution environment for a service (a system call)

ebreak.summary: Breakpoint: hand control to the debugger

lwu.summary: Load a word from rs1 + imm, zero-extended to 64 bits

sd.summary: Store the 64-bit value of rs2 at rs1 + imm

addiw.summary: 32-bit add of rs1 and imm, result sign-extended to 64 bits

slliw.summary: 32-bit shift left by a constant, result sign-extended to 64 bits

srliw.summary: 32-bit logical shift right by a constant, result sign-extended

sraiw.summary: 32-bit arithmetic shift right by a constant, result sign-extended

sllw.summary: 32-bit shift left by the low 5 bits of rs2, result sign-extended

srlw.summary: 32-bit logical shift right by the low 5 bits of rs2, result sign-extended

sraw.summary: 32-bit arithmetic shift right by the low 5 bits of rs2, result sign-extended

mul.summary: rd = low half of rs1 x rs2

mulh.summary: rd = high half of the signed x signed product

mulhsu.summary: rd = high half of the signed x unsigned product

mulhu.summary: rd = high half of the unsigned x unsigned product

div.summary: Signed division, rounded toward zero; dividing by zero gives -1

divu.summary: Unsigned division; dividing by zero gives all ones

rem.summary: Signed remainder, sign follows rs1; remainder by zero gives rs1

remu.summary: Unsigned remainder; remainder by zero gives rs1

flw.summary: Load a single-precision float from rs1 + imm

fsw.summary: Store the single-precision float in fs2 at rs1 + imm

fmadd.s.summary: fd = fs1 x fs2 + fs3 (single precision, one rounding)

fmsub.s.summary: fd = fs1 x fs2 - fs3 (single precision, one rounding)

fnmsub.s.summary: fd = -(fs1 x fs2) + fs3 (single precision, one rounding)

fnmadd.s.summary: fd = -(fs1 x fs2) - fs3 (single precision, one rounding)

fsqrt.s.summary: fd = square root of fs1 (single precision)

la.summary: Load the address of a data label: rd = &label
la.expandsTo: auipc rd, hi; addi rd, rd, lo

li.expandsTo: addi rd, x0, imm (or lui + addi for large values)

ret.summary: Return from a subroutine: jump to the address in ra

sext.w.summary: Sign-extend the low 32 bits of rs to 64 bits

bgt.summary: Branch to label if rs > rt (signed)

ble.summary: Branch to label if rs <= rt (signed)

bgtu.summary: Branch to label if rs > rt (unsigned)

bleu.summary: Branch to label if rs <= rt (unsigned)

j.summary: Jump to label without saving a return address

jr.summary: Jump to the address in rs

mulw.summary: 32-bit multiply of the low words, result sign-extended to 64 bits

divw.summary: 32-bit signed division of the low words, result sign-extended; dividing by zero gives -1

divuw.summary: 32-bit unsigned division of the low words, result sign-extended; dividing by zero gives all ones

remw.summary: 32-bit signed remainder of the low words, result sign-extended; remainder by zero gives rs1's low word

remuw.summary: 32-bit unsigned remainder of the low words, result sign-extended; remainder by zero gives rs1's low word

feq.d.summary: rd = 1 if fs1 == fs2, else 0 (0 if either is NaN)

flt.d.summary: rd = 1 if fs1 < fs2, else 0 (0 if either is NaN)

fle.d.summary: rd = 1 if fs1 <= fs2, else 0 (0 if either is NaN)

fmin.d.summary: fd = the smaller of fs1 and fs2; -0.0 counts as smaller than +0.0; if one operand is NaN the other is returned

fmax.d.summary: fd = the larger of fs1 and fs2; +0.0 counts as larger than -0.0; if one operand is NaN the other is returned

csrrw.summary: Swap: rd = old CSR value, then CSR = rs1

csrrs.summary: rd = old CSR value, then set every CSR bit that is set in rs1

csrrc.summary: rd = old CSR value, then clear every CSR bit that is set in rs1

csrrwi.summary: Like csrrw, but the value written is a 5-bit immediate

csrrsi.summary: Like csrrs, but the bits to set come from a 5-bit immediate

csrrci.summary: Like csrrc, but the bits to clear come from a 5-bit immediate

fence_i.summary: Synchronise the instruction stream with earlier stores

tail.summary: Tail call: jump to label without saving a return address
